claims.text: Air traffic controllers manage the movement of thousands of flights every day, balancing safety, efficiency and capacity.
claims.label: controllers managing thousands of daily flights

claims.text: The system relies heavily on radar technology, which tracks aircraft positions and speeds in real time.
claims.label: radar's real-time tracking

claims.text: Sophisticated computer systems predict potential conflicts and generate flight plans.
claims.label: computers predicting conflicts

claims.text: A flight plan, drafted by pilots and controllers, sets out the route, altitude, speed and headings an aircraft will follow.
claims.label: the contents of a flight plan

claims.text: Ground controllers, working in specialized centers, guide aircraft from the runway to take-off and keep departing planes separated.
claims.label: ground controllers at take-off

claims.text: Once airborne, an aircraft passes to en route air traffic control, where controllers monitor its progress and adjust its path.
claims.label: the en route hand-off

claims.text: Delays, weather conditions and airspace restrictions force controllers to reroute and prioritize flights.
claims.label: reroutes for weather and delays
